checks.reason: Both editions describe Bohr's quantitative success for hydrogen spectral-line positions without claiming all precision corrections are captured.
checks.primary_text: MIT-5.111-L6, energy-level and one-electron spectrum discussion.
checks.independent_reasoning: The one-electron Coulomb model supplies discrete leading-order hydrogen energies, so energy differences predict spectral positions.

checks.reason: Both editions correctly clarify the failure to obtain an equally reliable complete quantitative account of neutral helium and more complex atoms. This is not a claim that one-electron helium ions cannot be treated.
checks.independent_reasoning: Additional interacting electrons introduce coupled motion and correlations absent from the single-electron Bohr model. The source's important qualitative results are retained.
checks.raw_preservation: The awkward original wording remains unchanged in raw prose and both editions' provenance. It is not a newly authored translation error.

checks.reason: Both editions explain the mixture of classical dynamics and additional quantum postulates, place quantum mechanics in the 1920s, and say QED began developing then rather than being completely constructed then.
primary_texts: Tomonaga-Nobel-1966, opening discussion and its 1929 Heisenberg-Pauli reference; later covariant and postwar developments.
Feynman-Nobel-1965, opening account of unresolved theory and later work.
checks.independent_reasoning: Classical motion plus Coulomb attraction does not itself supply discrete stationary states or the quantum transition rule; a classical accelerating bound charge also presents a radiation problem. An early field-theory formulation does not establish completion of subsequent QED.

checks.reason: Both editions distinguish stationary states and transition frequencies from Bohr's particular orbit-quantization prescription, explicitly limiting the latter rather than declaring every orbit rule universally correct.
checks.primary_text: MIT-5.111-L6, stationary-state wavefunctions, quantum numbers, energy-level transitions and rejection of well-defined classical orbits.
checks.independent_reasoning: A stationary quantum state is not a radiating classical orbit. Its eigenenergy and transition energy explain the useful content of Bohr's postulates without requiring the old trajectory model.

checks.reason: Both editions deny a definite planetary electron path and define an electron cloud probabilistically. For hydrogen's lowest-energy state they explicitly separate the radial thin-shell probability maximum near the Bohr radius from the per-unit-volume probability-density maximum at the nucleus.
checks.primary_text: MIT-5.111-L6, lecture pages 3-5: volume-density definition, thin-shell weighting, hydrogen 1s most probable radius at the Bohr radius, and no well-defined electron orbits.
checks.independent_reasoning: The hydrogen 1s spatial density decreases outward from the nucleus. Equal-thickness shells have increasing area, so shell probability starts at zero at the origin, grows, then decays. Maximizing this shell-weighted ground-state distribution gives the Bohr radius. A density maximum at a point is not a nonzero probability of occupying exactly that point.
checks.qualification: The thin-shell radial-distribution wording is appropriate; it does not confuse a distribution with a point probability or a classical trajectory. The obsolete claim to answer any electron-cloud question is appropriately replaced by a framework with potentially difficult calculations.

checks.reason: The body rejects a motion trail; the matched footnote explicitly makes long exposure only an analogy for spatial distribution. Neither modern edition claims a literal exposure photograph of an orbital or everyday back-and-forth electron motion.
checks.independent_reasoning: A spatial probability distribution is not produced by tracking one classical path during a camera exposure. The footnote preserves precisely this limitation.

reference_and_formula_check.target: Top-level /prose/*/text in each of the three bound lessons

SCI.raw_science_note: Literal exposure language, the original density ambiguity, historical completion wording and the broad correctness claim survive only as faithfully retained source prose/provenance. SCI PASS approves their explicit modern clarifications, not those obsolete literal readings.

ZHEN.title: The English title faithfully names the difficulties of Bohr's theory and quantum mechanics.

paired_blocks.reason: Hydrogen spectral lines and their quantitative positions have the same clear meaning in Chinese and coherent English.

Helium and more complex atoms, retained qualitative value, and the limited complete quantitative account match. English does not literally reproduce the source's awkward atom wording as wrong science.
Internal inconsistency, Newtonian mechanics, Coulomb's law, non-derived quantum postulates, the 1920s and QED beginning to develop are equivalent.
Stationary states, energy-difference radiation frequencies and the limited approximation domain of Bohr orbit quantization retain the same scientific qualifications.

No planetary path, a probabilistic electron cloud, the ground-state thin-shell versus volume-density distinction, the same old reference and the introductory learning scope all match. English is scientifically coherent rather than a literal mistranslation.
The same footnote limits long exposure to an analogy and denies everyday path motion. Its callout remains attached to the electron-cloud block.

identity_and_provenance.reason: Bohr remains Bohr; Newtonian mechanics and Coulomb's law retain the same identities. No fictional person or historical substitution occurs. Maxwell remains in unmodified raw source/provenance; both modern versions simplify that sentence without attributing electromagnetism to somebody else.

style_preferences_not_errors: Spelling out nineteen-twenties and the footnote-marker spacing are not meaning defects and require no change.

overall_rule: PASS only because SCI and ZHEN are both independently settled PASS.

method_and_limits.authority: The human's review scope, the bound source-pass record, the actual final raw/modern texts, readable primary physics text, and independent physics reasoning.
